common_name: Italia Pepper (Corno di Toro-Type Sweet Frying Pepper)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before transplanting; Italia is an early corno di toro-type Italian frying pepper, and its compact, upright habit makes it a good choice for smaller beds or containers.

directions: Italia is a corno di toro-type sweet pepper introduced to American gardeners by Johnny's Selected Seeds in 1987, with curved, tapering fruit that looks like a long hot pepper but carries no heat at all. Plants are upright and not very branching, reaching a modest 14-28 inches, and set long (5-8 inch) thin-walled pods that can be picked green as early as 55 days after transplant or left to ripen to red by 70-80 days for fuller sweetness. The sweet, thin flesh is well suited to frying in olive oil, roasting, and fresh eating, in keeping with traditional Italian frying-pepper use. Its early maturity and compact size make it a practical option for gardeners with limited space or shorter growing seasons.
